chapter: Southwestern bands and New Orleans youth
title: George Moret, rough New Orleans trumpeter
summary: Moret lived near Albert's family, read music and played loud and rough; Albert went on jobs with him at ten or twelve.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Buddy Bolden and Buddy Petit: the trumpet legends

blocks.x: Back to New Orleans in the early days, what did George Moret sound like?

George Moret was a rough, well, I'll explain it in musical terms, a rough trumpet player. Very good musician. Old man George Moret lived about three or four blocks from my house in the family. Real close friends through my grandfather and my father. And George could read music and actually he came from the old school or the old professors too. But he was loud and rough, if I can recall real well. Because when I went to, when George would take me on the jobs with him, I was only in the area of a lot of ten, twelve years old.
Do you remember him as playing any jazz or remember him as a brass band? Well, yes.
Mostly like they played in Manu Perez and guys like that played practically the same type of trumpet.
Do you remember who was in George Moret's bands?
No, I can't recall anybody there. Unless someone would refresh my memory of it, then I could remember.
